chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"The daughters of the daughter stand in the place of the daughter if the deceased has no daughters and no other heir besides them, and the daughters of the son stand in the place of the son if the deceased has no offspring and no other heir besides them."

key_terms.بَنَاتُ اَلْاِبْنِ: Daughters of the son (paternal granddaughters via male line)
key_terms.بَنَاتُ اَلْبِنْتِ: Daughters of the daughter (paternal granddaughters via female line)
key_terms.يَقُمْنَ مَقَامَ: Stand in the place of / represent

ai.seo_question: How do granddaughters inherit in Shia Islamic law when there are no direct children?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the mechanism of *qadam al-bint* (standing in the place of), distinguishing between the daughter's daughter who inherits only in the absence of other daughters, and the son's daughter who inherits in the absence of any male or female descendants. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance where the son's line takes precedence in representation, ensuring the estate remains within the direct paternal lineage when possible, while the maternal line serves as a secondary substitute.
